# stem-calc-student-mcp

> STEM Calc MCP does the arithmetic of chemistry and physics homework with tested code: molar mass, balancing equations, grams to moles to particles, unit conversion and significant figures. It runs offline on your computer. No API key, no account.

## Setup
- Run with npx -y stem-calc-student-mcp
- Works with Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code and Windsurf. Needs Node.js 20 or newer.
- All five tools are read only. They calculate an answer and never change anything.

## Tools
- molar_mass: Parse a chemical formula and return the molar mass in g/mol with the mass each element adds. Handles brackets and hydrates like CuSO4.5H2O. Example prompt: "What is the molar mass of Ca(OH)2?"
- balance_equation: Balance a chemical equation written with -> and +. Example prompt: "Balance C3H8 + O2 -> CO2 + H2O."
- stoichiometry: Convert between grams, moles and particles. Converting to or from grams needs the chemical formula. Example prompt: "How many moles are in 36 grams of water?"
- convert_units: Convert a value between units of length, mass, time, volume, energy or temperature. It refuses to convert one kind of unit into another. Example prompt: "Convert 2.5 km to feet."
- round_sig_figs: Round a number to a given number of significant figures. Example prompt: "Round 123456 to 3 significant figures."

## Limits
- It knows 56 common elements. An unknown element symbol is an error.
- It does not find limiting reagents and does not handle charges or isotopes.
- Units are written as m, km, cm, mm, in, ft, g, kg, mg, lb, s, min, h, L, mL, m^3, J, kJ, cal, kcal, K, C and F.

## Answers to common questions
- "What is the molar mass of copper sulfate pentahydrate?" Use molar_mass with CuSO4.5H2O.
- "Can it balance any equation?" It balances equations that have a solution and says so when it cannot.
- "Does it need the internet?" No. Everything is calculated on your computer.
